name: Teclistamab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection with step-up dosing, then weekly or every 2 weeks
originator: Janssen (Johnson & Johnson), using Genmab DuoBody technology

discovery.note: Humanised IgG4 bispecific antibody binding B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) and CD3.

tagline: First BCMA-directed bispecific antibody for relapsed multiple myeloma
summary: Teclistamab is a bispecific antibody that binds BCMA on myeloma cells and CD3 on T cells, redirecting T cells to kill myeloma cells. It is approved for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after several prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory drug and an anti-CD38 antibody.
mechanism: Teclistamab engages CD3 on T cells and BCMA (TNFRSF17), a receptor expressed on malignant and normal plasma cells, forming a cytolytic synapse.
T-cell activation leads to release of perforin and granzymes, lysis of myeloma cells and cytokine release. Step-up dosing reduces the severity of cytokine release syndrome.
uses: Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after at least three (US: four) prior lines including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent and an anti-CD38 antibody

history.title: MajesTEC-1
history.detail: First results of the pivotal phase 1/2 study show durable responses in heavily pretreated myeloma.

history.title: EU conditional approval
history.detail: The EU grants conditional approval in August, the first approval anywhere.

history.title: FDA accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA approves Tecvayli in October with a REMS programme for CRS and neurotoxicity.

history.title: Longer-term data
history.detail: Follow-up of MajesTEC-1 supports less frequent (every 2 weeks) dosing in responders.

history.title: MajesTEC-3
history.detail: Teclistamab plus daratumumab improves progression-free survival over standard regimens in earlier relapsed myeloma.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

safety.boxed_warning: Cytokine release syndrome and neurological toxicity including immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS).

facts: Teclistamab was the first BCMA × CD3 bispecific antibody approved.
Infection risk is high because normal plasma cells are also depleted, causing hypogammaglobulinaemia.
